name: Texas

agency.name: Texas Department of Public Safety, Driver License Division

knowledgeTest.format: Class C knowledge exam taken during the classroom portion of an approved driver education course or at a DPS driver license office
knowledgeTest.languages: English or Spanish (DPS states road signs written in English must be understood to pass)
knowledgeTest.retestWait: No waiting period stated. If you fail the knowledge or driving exam, your application is held for 90 days; after 90 days or three failed exams, a new application and fee are required.
knowledgeTest.notes: The handbook says you must score 70 percent or better to pass any knowledge exam (Texas Driver Handbook p. 13). DPS does not publish the number of questions on its website. Teens (15-17) take the knowledge exam during driver ed classroom instruction or at a DPS office before getting a learner license. All applicants under 25 must take driver education; on completing certain courses they need not take the Class C knowledge exam at the office. Applicants 18+ who surrender a valid out-of-state license are exempt from the knowledge and driving exams.

motorcycleTest.notes: The Class M knowledge exam is waived for applicants who complete a TDLR-approved motorcycle safety course (completion certificate valid 24 months). All applicants under 18 must pass a DPS-administered motorcycle skills test. A 15-year-old is limited to motorcycles of 250 cc or less. The 70% pass mark applies to any knowledge exam per the handbook (p. 13).

facts.value: 0.08% BAC (age 21 and over)
facts.detail: A driver 21 or older is legally intoxicated at a BAC of 0.08 or more, or at any level that causes loss of normal use of mental or physical faculties.

source.quote: In Texas, a person, age 21 and over, is considered legally intoxicated if the person has a BAC of 0.08 or more.

facts.value: Any detectable amount (zero tolerance)
facts.detail: Texas zero tolerance: a driver under 21 with any detectable amount of alcohol commits Driving Under the Influence by a Minor, even if not legally intoxicated.

source.quote: Texas law does not allow any amount of blood alcohol concentration (BAC) for minors.

facts.value: 0.04% BAC in a commercial motor vehicle
facts.detail: Operating a CMV at a BAC of .04% or more is illegal and a first offense costs the CDL for at least one year.

source.quote: It is illegal to operate a CMV if your blood alcohol concentration (BAC) is .04% or more.

facts.value: Refusal: license suspended 180 days (up to 730 days for later offenses)
facts.detail: Refusing a breath or blood test brings a 180-day suspension (up to 730 days for subsequent offenses). A failed test (0.08+) can bring a 90-day suspension (up to 365 days for subsequent offenses).

source.quote: A person who refuses to give a blood or breath specimen for analysis will have their driver license suspended for 180 days or up to 730 days for subsequent offenses.

facts.value: Fine up to $2,000; 72 hours to 180 days in jail; license suspended 90 to 365 days
facts.detail: First DWI for an adult: fine up to $2,000, 72 hours to 180 days in jail, and a 90-day to 365-day license suspension.

source.quote: 1st offense Up to $2,000 72 hours to 180 days in jail 90 days to 365 days

facts.value: Illegal in the passenger area on a public highway, even if parked; fine up to $500
facts.detail: An open container of alcohol in the passenger area is illegal whether the vehicle is moving, stopped, or parked on a public highway. Fine not to exceed $500.

source.quote: It is illegal to possess an open container of alcohol in a motor vehicle passenger area located on a public highway, regardless of whether the vehicle is being operated, stopped, or parked. Conviction of this offense is punishable by a fine not to exceed $500.

facts.detail: A learner license (instruction permit) requires age 15 to 18, the classroom portion of driver education, a vision exam and a knowledge exam.

source.quote: Be at least 15 but no more than 18 years of age

facts.value: 6 months
facts.detail: Phase One of the GDL program: hold a learner (or hardship) license for at least six months before a provisional license. Any suspension extends the six months by the days suspended.

source.quote: A Texas learner license must be held for six months from the date of issuance before the individual is eligible for Phase Two.

facts.value: 30 hours of behind-the-wheel practice, at least 10 at night
facts.detail: Before a provisional license, teens complete 30 hours of behind-the-wheel practice (at least 10 at night) with a licensed driver 21 or older, in addition to 7 hours of in-car observation and 7 hours of in-car driving with the driver education instructor.

source.quote: 30 hours of behind the wheel driving practice, of which at least 10 hours must be at night with a licensed driver 21 years of age or older in the vehicle at all times.

facts.value: Licensed driver 21+ with at least 1 year of driving experience, in the front passenger seat
facts.detail: The supervising driver must be at least 21, have at least one year of driving experience, sit beside the learner, and must not be intoxicated, asleep, or otherwise unable to observe and respond.

source.quote: The licensed driver must be at least 21 years of age with at least one year of driving experience, must occupy the seat beside the driver, and cannot be intoxicated, asleep, or engaging in any activity that prevents observation and response to the actions of the driver.

facts.detail: A provisional license (Phase Two) is issued at 16 to 18 after driver education, a vision and driving exam, and holding a learner license for at least six months. It expires on the 18th birthday.

source.quote: Be at least 16 but not more than 18 years of age

facts.value: No driving midnight to 5:00 a.m. (exceptions: work, school activity, medical emergency)
facts.detail: Provisional drivers under 18 may not drive between midnight and 5 a.m. unless driving is necessary for work, a school-related activity, or a medical emergency.

source.quote: Between midnight and 5:00 a.m. unless the operation of the vehicle is necessary for the driver to work, to attend or participate in a school-related activity, or due to a medical emergency

facts.value: No more than 1 passenger under 21 who is not a family member
facts.detail: Provisional drivers under 18 may not carry more than one passenger under 21 who is not a family member.

source.quote: With more than one passenger in the vehicle under the age of 21 who is not a family member

facts.detail: Phase Two (provisional) restrictions last until the 18th birthday, when the provisional license expires.

source.quote: Phase Two restricts the driving privileges of individuals until their 18th birthday following the issuance of a provisional license.

facts.value: No general statewide handheld ban; in a school crossing zone a wireless device may be used only with a hands-free device or while stopped
facts.detail: Texas Transportation Code 545.425 bans using a wireless communication device while driving in a school crossing zone unless the vehicle is stopped or a hands-free device is used. The handbook shows a sign saying wireless device use is prohibited in the school zone.

source.quote: an operator may not use a wireless communication device while operating a motor vehicle within a school crossing zone, as defined by Section 541.302, Transportation Code, unless:

facts.value: Reading, writing, or sending messages on a portable wireless device while driving is illegal for all drivers
facts.detail: Texting while driving is against the law for all drivers. A phone may be used to contact law enforcement or in an emergency; pull off the road safely to make a call.

source.quote: It is against the law to read, write, or send messages on a cell phone or other portable wireless device.

facts.value: Drivers under 18 may not use any wireless device, even hands-free, except in an emergency
facts.detail: All drivers under 18, including learner and provisional license holders, are barred from wireless communication devices, including hands-free devices, except in an emergency.

source.quote: All drivers who are under 18 years of age are restricted from using a wireless communication device, including a hands-free device, except in case of an emergency.

facts.value: Driver and all passengers of every age must be belted
facts.detail: Everyone in a seat equipped with a safety belt must wear it. The driver is fined $100-$200 for each passenger under 17 who is unbelted. Anyone 15 or older can be cited for not wearing a belt.

source.quote: The driver and all passengers, regardless of age, in a passenger vehicle are required to use safety belts if occupying a seat in a vehicle equipped with a safety belt.

facts.value: Child under 8 must be in a child safety seat unless taller than 4 feet 9 inches
facts.detail: Children under 8 must ride in a federally approved child safety seat unless they are more than 4'9" tall. Fine $25-$250.

source.quote: Any child under 8 years old must be secured in a federally approved child car seat if occupying a seat in a vehicle equipped with a safety belt, unless the child is more than 4’9” tall.

facts.value: Never drive faster than is safe and prudent for conditions, regardless of the posted limit
facts.detail: Posted limits are for normal conditions. In heavy traffic, bad weather, or low visibility you must drive slower than the limit.

source.quote: basic speed law – you may not drive faster than is safe and prudent for existing conditions, regardless of posted speed limits

facts.value: As posted on the school zone sign; in effect when the yellow light is flashing
facts.detail: Texas school zone limits are posted locally. The posted school zone speed applies while the sign's yellow light flashes.

source.quote: School Zone: The speed shown is in effect when the yellow light is flashing.

facts.value: 30 mph (urban district)
facts.detail: The statewide speed limit in an urban district (areas built up with homes or businesses) is 30 mph unless otherwise posted; alleys are 15 mph.

source.quote: Urban District 30 Alley 15

facts.value: 30 mph (urban district)
facts.detail: Business areas fall under the urban district limit of 30 mph unless otherwise posted.

source.quote: Urban District 30

facts.value: 70 mph on Texas/U.S.-numbered highways outside urban districts; 60 mph on unnumbered highways
facts.detail: Outside an urban district, the limit for passenger cars is 70 mph on highways numbered by Texas or the U.S. (including Farm to Market and Ranch to Market roads) and 60 mph on highways that are not numbered.

source.quote: Highway numbered by Texas or the U.S. outside an urban district including Farm to Market and Ranch to Market roads

facts.value: Up to 85 mph where posted
facts.detail: Many limited-access highways are posted at 75 mph and up to 85 mph. Always obey the posted limit.

source.quote: Many limited access highways have speed limits of 75 up to 85 mph.

facts.value: Obey posted minimum speeds; if you cannot drive at or above the minimum, do not use the highway
facts.detail: Drivers must obey posted minimum speed limits. The right lane is for driving at the minimum speed or below the normal flow of traffic.

source.quote: If you cannot or do not want to drive at or above the minimum speed limit, do not use the highway.

facts.value: Allowed after a complete stop unless prohibited
facts.detail: At a steady red light, stop before the crosswalk or intersection, then you may turn right unless a sign prohibits it, yielding to pedestrians and other traffic.

source.quote: Stop before entering the crosswalk or intersection. You may turn right unless prohibited by law.

facts.value: Allowed after stopping only from a one-way street onto a one-way street, unless prohibited
facts.detail: A left turn on a steady red is legal only when both streets are one-way, after stopping and yielding to pedestrians and traffic.

source.quote: You may also turn left if both streets are one way, unless prohibited by law.

facts.value: At least 100 feet before turning or stopping
facts.detail: Signal continuously for at least 100 feet before turning or stopping, and cancel the signal after the turn.

source.quote: Signal continuously for at least 100 feet before turning or stopping

facts.value: Pull to the right edge and stop; do not follow within 500 feet of a fire truck or ambulance with flashing lights
facts.detail: Yield to emergency vehicles using a siren, bell, or flashing red light by pulling to the right edge and stopping (or slowing and leaving a clear path). Do not follow within 500 feet of a fire truck answering an alarm or an ambulance with flashing red lights.

source.quote: You are not allowed to follow within 500 feet of a fire truck answering an alarm or an ambulance when the flashing red lights are on.

facts.value: Vacate the lane next to a stopped emergency vehicle, or slow to 20 mph below the limit (to under 5 mph if the limit is below 25 mph)
facts.detail: For a stopped emergency, police, fire, tow, utility service, or TxDOT vehicle with lights on: vacate the lane closest to it on a road with two or more lanes in that direction, or slow to 20 mph below a posted limit of 25 mph or more (slow to less than 5 mph if the posted limit is under 25 mph).

source.quote: Slow to a speed not more than 20 mph less than the posted speed limit when the posted speed limit is 25 mph or more

facts.value: Stop from either direction for a bus with flashing red lights; no stop needed for a bus on a different roadway or in a controlled-access highway loading zone
facts.detail: Stop for a school bus with alternately flashing red lights from either direction and wait until it moves, the driver signals you, or the lights stop. You need not stop for a bus on a different road (Transportation Code 545.066: a highway with separate roadways, not merely a left-turn lane) or one in a controlled-access highway loading zone where pedestrians may not cross. First offense: $500-$1,250.

source.quote: It is not necessary to stop when passing a school bus on a different road or when on a controlled-access highway where the bus is stopped in a loading zone and pedestrians aren’t permitted to cross.

facts.value: 2 seconds at 30 mph or less; 4 seconds above 30 mph (good conditions)
facts.detail: Keep at least 2 seconds behind at speeds of 30 mph or less and 4 seconds above 30 mph in good conditions. Allow more in poor conditions; 4 seconds is best practice for beginners.

source.quote: For speeds 30 mph or less, the minimum time between your car and the one in front of you is 2 seconds with good road conditions. For speeds above 30 mph, maintain a 4 second gap between cars during good road conditions.

facts.value: 30 minutes after sunset to 30 minutes before sunrise, or when you can't see 1,000 feet
facts.detail: Headlights are required from 30 minutes after sunset until 30 minutes before sunrise, and whenever people or vehicles cannot be seen clearly for at least 1,000 feet.

source.quote: You must use your headlights beginning 30 minutes after sunset and ending 30 minutes before sunrise, or anytime when individuals or vehicles cannot be seen clearly for at least 1,000 feet.

facts.value: Within 500 feet of an approaching vehicle
facts.detail: Switch to low beams when within 500 feet of an oncoming vehicle.

source.quote: Within 500 feet of an approaching vehicle

facts.value: Within 300 feet behind another vehicle
facts.detail: Use low beams when following within 300 feet of another vehicle.

source.quote: Following closely (within 300 feet) behind another vehicle

facts.value: 15 feet
facts.detail: Do not park or stand within 15 feet of a fire hydrant, occupied or not.

source.quote: Within 15 feet of a fire hydrant

facts.value: 20 feet of a crosswalk at an intersection
facts.detail: Do not park or stand within 20 feet of a crosswalk at an intersection. Never park on a crosswalk.

source.quote: Within 20 feet of a crosswalk at an intersection

facts.value: Never within an intersection (and not within 20 feet of a crosswalk at an intersection)
facts.detail: Stopping, standing, or parking within an intersection is prohibited. Combined with the crosswalk rule, stay at least 20 feet back from a crosswalk at an intersection.

source.quote: Within an intersection

facts.value: 30 feet on the approach to a flashing signal, stop sign, yield sign, or traffic signal
facts.detail: Do not park or stand within 30 feet on the approach to a flashing signal, stop sign, yield sign, or other traffic control signal at the side of the road.

source.quote: Within 30 feet upon the approach to any flashing signal, stop sign, yield sign, or other traffic control signal located at the side of a road

facts.value: 50 feet from the nearest rail
facts.detail: Do not park within 50 feet of the nearest rail of a railroad crossing, occupied or not.

source.quote: Do not park a vehicle, occupied or not, within 50 feet of the nearest rail of a railroad crossing.

facts.value: 20 feet of the driveway entrance; 75 feet on the opposite side of the street
facts.detail: Do not park within 20 feet of a fire station driveway entrance, or within 75 feet of the entrance on the opposite side of the street.

source.quote: Within 20 feet of the driveway entrance to any fire station and on the side of a street opposite the entrance to any fire station within 75 feet of entrance

facts.value: No more than 18 inches from the curb
facts.detail: When parallel parking, end about six inches from the curb and never more than 18 inches from the curb or edge of the road.

source.quote: Do not park more than 18 inches from the curb or edge of the road.

facts.value: Between 15 and 50 feet from the nearest rail
facts.detail: When a signal, lowered gate, flagger, or approaching train requires a stop at a railroad crossing, stop between 15 and 50 feet from the nearest rail.

source.quote: When approaching a railroad grade crossing, stop between 15 and 50 feet from the nearest rail if:

facts.value: Yield to pedestrians at uncontrolled intersections, with a WALK signal, on green, and to those already in the crosswalk when the light changes
facts.detail: Drivers must yield to pedestrians at uncontrolled intersections and to those with a WALK signal (or green light with no pedestrian signal), even if the light changes after they enter the crosswalk. Pedestrians crossing outside a crosswalk at an intersection must yield to vehicles.

source.quote: If the light changes after the pedestrian has entered the crosswalk, still give the pedestrian the right-of-way.

facts.value: Immediately notify police of a crash with injury, death, or a vehicle that cannot be safely driven
facts.detail: Transportation Code 550.026 requires the driver to immediately notify the local police (or sheriff/DPS outside a city) when a crash causes injury or death or leaves a vehicle unable to be normally and safely driven. The handbook also advises notifying police when a driver leaves the scene or you suspect intoxication.

source.quote: The operator of a vehicle involved in a collision resulting in injury to or death of a person or damage to a vehicle to the extent that it cannot be normally and safely driven shall immediately by the quickest means of communication give notice of the collision

facts.detail: Minimum liability insurance: $30,000 for injury or death of one person, $60,000 for two or more people, and $25,000 for property damage.

source.quote: $30,000 against injury or death of one person • $60,000 against injury or death of two or more individuals • $25,000 against property damage

facts.value: No point system in the handbook; DPS may suspend for 4+ convictions in 12 months or 7+ in 24 months
facts.detail: The handbook describes no point system. DPS may suspend a license after a hearing for repeated violations: four or more traffic convictions in any 12 months or seven or more in any 24 months. Drivers under 18 face suspension for two or more convictions in 12 months.

source.quote: Four or more traffic convictions occurring separately within any 12-month period

facts.value: Helmet required for riders and passengers under 21; those 21+ are exempt only with a training course or qualifying health insurance
facts.detail: Every motorcycle operator and passenger must wear approved protective headgear unless at least 21 and either has completed a motorcycle operator training and safety course or is covered by health insurance for motorcycle crash injuries.

source.quote: the person required to wear protective headgear was at least 21 years old and had successfully completed a motorcycle operator training and safety course under Chapter 662 or was covered by a health insurance plan providing the person with medical benefits for injuries incurred as a result of a collision while operating or riding on a motorcycle.

facts.value: Prohibited
facts.detail: Transportation Code 545.0605 (since Sept. 1, 2023): a motorcyclist may not ride between lanes of traffic moving in the same direction, may ride at most two abreast in one lane, and may not pass a vehicle in the same lane. A motorcycle is entitled to the full use of a lane.

source.quote: operate the motorcycle between lanes of traffic moving in the same direction

notableLaws.title: Frontage road traffic yields to vehicles entering or leaving the highway
notableLaws.summary: On a controlled-access highway's frontage road, you must yield to vehicles leaving the highway onto the frontage road and to vehicles leaving the frontage road to enter the highway.

source.quote: The driver traveling on a frontage road of a controlled-access highway must yield the right-of-way to a vehicle: • Entering or about to enter the frontage road from the highway; and • Leaving or about to leave the frontage road to enter the highway.

notableLaws.title: Smaller road yields to a divided or 3+ lane road
notableLaws.summary: A driver on a single- or two-lane road meeting a divided road or a road with three or more lanes must yield to traffic on the larger road.

source.quote: If you are driving on a single or two lane road that intersects with a divided road or road with three (3) or more lanes, you must yield the right-of-way to vehicles traveling on the divided or three (3) or more lane road.

notableLaws.title: Unpaved road yields to paved road
notableLaws.summary: Drivers on an unpaved road must yield to vehicles on the paved road they are entering or crossing.

source.quote: If you are driving on an unpaved road that intersects with a paved road, you must yield the right-of-way to vehicles traveling on the paved road.

notableLaws.title: Fines double in work zones when workers are present
notableLaws.summary: Disobeying warning signs or driving around a barricade carries a $1-$200 fine, doubled in a construction or maintenance zone when workers are present.

source.quote: Fines double in a construction or maintenance work zone when workers are present anywhere in the construction zone.

notableLaws.title: Driving around a high-water barricade is a Class B misdemeanor
notableLaws.summary: Ignoring a warning sign or barricade placed where water is over the road is a Class B misdemeanor: up to $2,000 fine and/or up to 180 days in jail.

source.quote: The offense is a Class B misdemeanor punishable by a fine of up to $2,000 and/or up to 180 days in jail when a warning sign or barricade has been placed at a location where water is over any portion of a road, street, or highway.

notableLaws.title: Disabled parking violation: $500-$750 first offense
notableLaws.summary: Parking, standing, or stopping in a disabled space without a disabled plate or placard is a misdemeanor with a $500-$750 fine for a first offense, rising to $1,250 for five or more offenses.

source.quote: Illegally parking in a space reserved for individuals with disabilities is a misdemeanor punishable by a fine of $500 to $750 for the first offense.

notableLaws.title: Left lane is for passing only where signed
notableLaws.summary: Where the 'Left Lane for Passing Only' sign is posted on multi-lane roads, slower traffic must use a lane other than the farthest left lane.

source.quote: slower traffic should travel in a lane other than the farthest left lane. The farthest left lane is for passing only.

notableLaws.title: No driving on the left within 100 feet of intersections, railroad crossings, bridges, or tunnels
notableLaws.summary: You may not drive on the left side of the road within 100 feet of an intersection or railroad crossing, or within 100 feet of a bridge, viaduct, or tunnel.

source.quote: Within 100 feet of or crossing an intersection or railroad crossing

notableLaws.title: Passing on a paved shoulder is allowed in limited cases
notableLaws.summary: You may pass on the right using a paved shoulder when the vehicle ahead is slowing or stopped on the main road, disabled, or preparing to turn left. Never pass on the right by leaving the pavement.

source.quote: You may pass on a paved shoulder when the vehicle you are passing is slowing or stopped on the main traveled portion of the highway, disabled, or preparing to make a left turn.

notableLaws.title: No children under 18 in an open truck bed
notableLaws.summary: It is an offense to drive an open-bed or open flatbed truck, or pull an open flatbed trailer, while a child younger than 18 rides in the bed. Limited defenses apply, such as parades, emergencies, and beaches.

source.quote: It is an offense to drive an open bed truck, an open flatbed truck, or to draw an open flatbed trailer when a child who is younger than 18 years of age is occupying the bed of the truck or trailer.

notableLaws.title: Move drivable vehicles off the main lanes after a damage-only crash
notableLaws.summary: If a crash causes only vehicle damage on a freeway main lane, ramp, shoulder, or median and the vehicles can be driven safely, move them as soon as possible to a crash investigation site, the frontage road, a nearby cross street, or another suitable place (Transportation Code 550.022 applies this to freeways in metropolitan areas).

source.quote: If the crash occurs on a main lane, ramp, shoulder, median, or adjacent area and each vehicle involved can be normally and safely driven, drivers must move their vehicle as soon as possible to a designated crash investigation site, if available, a location on the frontage road, the nearest suitable cross street, or other suitable location.

notableLaws.title: Knowledge exams require 70 percent
notableLaws.summary: Every Texas knowledge exam (Class C, Class M, Class A/B rules) requires a score of 70 percent or better.

source.quote: You must score a grade of 70 percent or better to pass any knowledge exam.

gaps: bicycle_passing: neither the handbook, an official DPS page, nor Transportation Code ch. 545 (checked Oct 2026) states a minimum distance for passing a bicycle; the handbook only says a bicycle is a vehicle with the same rights and that motorists should merge with bicycle traffic before a right turn.

knowledgeTest.questions/passingScore: no official DPS page (testing-other-languages, apply, learner, FAQ pages re-checked Oct 2026) or the handbook states how many questions are on the Class C knowledge exam; only the 70% pass mark is official.
officialPracticeTests: DPS does not publish an online practice test; the handbook's Appendix C has open-ended study questions only.

crash_reporting: handbook p. 65 still says drivers must file a written crash report with TxDOT within 10 days when no officer investigates, but that driver-report statute (former Transportation Code 550.061) was repealed effective Sept. 1, 2017 (Sec. 550.065 refers to 'former Section 550.061 ... before September 1, 2017'). The 10-day driver report is therefore not used; only the immediate police-notice rule (Sec. 550.026) is.
